record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Qualitative comparison of explicit versus implicit map dynamics
record.original_question: Whenever spatially non-constant steady states exist for the system ∂_t u_i = d_iΔu_i − γ_i∇·(u_i∇p_i g,R), ∂_t p_i = Σ_j=1^n α_ij u_j − μp_i, what qualitative properties do they have, and how do those properties compare with the steady states of the simpler model whose advection potential is based directly on perceived population densities Σ_j γ_ij u_j g,R? More generally, does explicitly modeling the cognitive map p_i create new dynamics not already present in the direct-density model?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 8. What are the qualitative characteristics of the spatially non-constant steady state solutions obtained for problem (2.11), whenever they exist? How do these qualitative properties compare to steady state solutions of model (2.10)? Of particular interest is the following general question: are the dynamics of model (2.11) included in the dynamics of model (2.10)? In other words, are new dynamics observed when the complexity is increased through explicit description of the cognitive map?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a smooth bounded domain (or, alternatively, take $\Omega=\mathbb{R}^N$ with suitable decay assumptions), and let $n\ge 1$ be an integer representing the number of interacting populations. For each $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, let $u_i(x,t)\ge 0$ denote the population density of species $i$ and let $p_i(x,t)$ denote a scalar "cognitive map" associated with species $i$. Fix positive constants $d_i,\gamma_i,\mu>0$, real coupling constants $\alpha_{ij}$ (for $i,j\in\{1,\dots,n\}$), and a nonlocal averaging kernel $g_R$ supported in a ball of radius $R>0$ (for instance the normalized indicator of $B_R(0)$). For a function $f$ on $\Omega$ define the nonlocal average
$$ (f\,{}_g\!*_R)(x) \;=\; \int g_R(x-y)\, f(y)\, dy. $$

Consider the coupled system (with no-flux or appropriate boundary conditions)
$$ \text{(I)}\qquad \begin{cases} \partial_t u_i \;=\; d_i\Delta u_i \;-\; \gamma_i\,\nabla\!\cdot\!\bigl(u_i\,\nabla(p_i\,{}_g\!*_R)\bigr), \\[2pt] \partial_t p_i \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^n \alpha_{ij} u_j \;-\; \mu p_i, \end{cases}\qquad i=1,\dots,n, $$
in which the advection of $u_i$ is driven by a nonlocally perceived cognitive map $p_i$ whose evolution is itself coupled to the population densities. Consider also the simpler "direct-density" model in which the cognitive map is replaced by an instantaneous, weighted, nonlocally perceived combination of densities:
$$ \text{(II)}\qquad \partial_t u_i \;=\; d_i\Delta u_i \;-\; \nabla\!\cdot\!\Bigl(u_i\,\nabla\bigl(\textstyle\sum_{j=1}^n \gamma_{ij}\, u_j\,{}_g\!*_R\bigr)\Bigr),\qquad i=1,\dots,n, $$
with coefficients $\gamma_{ij}$ that may be chosen to make (II) the natural quasi-steady limit of (I) (e.g.\ $\gamma_{ij}=\gamma_i\alpha_{ij}/\mu$).

Address the following questions:

(a) Whenever (I) admits spatially non-constant steady-state solutions, determine their qualitative properties: existence, multiplicity, regularity, monotonicity or symmetry, spatial profile (e.g.\ peaks, plateaus, aggregation patterns), stability, and dependence on the parameters $d_i,\gamma_i,\alpha_{ij},\mu,R$ and on the kernel $g_R$.

(b) Carry out the same analysis for the spatially non-constant steady states of (II) and compare with those of (I): identify which qualitative features (number of patterns, bifurcation structure, stability, asymptotic behavior, pattern shape) are preserved, modified, or lost when passing from (I) to (II).

(c) Determine whether the full dynamical behavior of (I) is contained in that of (II), in the sense that every long-time pattern, bifurcation, or attractor exhibited by (I) corresponds to one of (II) under a suitable identification of parameters. Equivalently, decide whether the explicit description of the cognitive map $p_i$ produces genuinely new dynamical phenomena (e.g.\ Hopf bifurcations, oscillatory patterns, hysteresis, additional steady-state branches) that cannot occur for (II).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question concerning a class of nonlocal cognitive-map PDE systems. A targeted web search did not surface a paper resolving the qualitative comparison between the cognitive-map model (I) and the direct-density model (II), nor a result showing that the dynamics of (I) are or are not contained in those of (II). The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement
status_evidence.snippet: Lists qualitative-properties comparison between cognitive-map and direct-density nonlocal advection-diffusion models as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The qualitative comparison and inclusion-of-dynamics question is stated as an unresolved open problem.
